newsitem.title: NIGERIA: New decree gives Nigeria's Abacha extra powers.
newsitem.headline: New decree gives Nigeria's Abacha extra powers.

text.p: A new Nigerian decree gives military ruler General Sani Abacha absolute power over local governments recently elected under a much-criticised plan to restore democracy, newspapers reported on Thursday.
They said the decree on local councils elected last month was issued by the ruling military council on Wednesday.

The semi-official Daily Times said under the decree head of state could remove any local council head if he "is satisfied that the affairs of the council are not being managed in the best interest of the community or in any way to strengthen the unity of the people of Nigeria".
The decree says no civil court can challenge the validity of the election or the decision of a special election tribunal.

Nigeria's ruling generals hold up the peaceful conduct of the local elections as a sign of popular support for their plan to restore civilian rule by October 1998, despite criticism from pro-democracy campaigners.

The March ballot was the first multiparty election in Nigeria since a former military government annuled 1993 elections that would have ended 10 years of army rule and paved the way for Abacha to take over in ensuing political chaos.

At least two of five political parties permitted under the transition to democracy are actively seeking the infantry general as a candidate for the 1998 elections, although he has not yet said he will stand.
